title: A let-go object on the Moon still returns to the ground
summary: The Moon has gravity. Let something go there and it returns to the ground instead of drifting upward.
body: NASA Science's Top Moon Questions page, updated 12 February 2026, answers a direct question: does the Moon have gravity, and do things float up when released? The answer is that the Moon does have gravity, and a released object does not float up. It comes back to the lunar ground. How much weaker that tug is, and how high a jump would go, are the next sentences on the page and are not this claim. A fact-sheet figure in metres per second squared lives on another card.
